_note: Derived by scripts/derive_usaspending_evidence.py from USAspending's own agency and bureau lists, committed verbatim under tests/fixtures/usaspending/ with their digests, for the organisations the phase-2 crosswalk (data/audit/nominations/cost-cost-usaspending.jsonl) names by a key the API prints for the same canonical name. Each record is File A gross_outlays -- gross, fiscal-year-to-date as of the fetch, and a different measure from the Monthly Treasury Statement's net line the graph publishes as a node's cost; the exporter stamps it beside that figure and never over it. A proposed key whose name the API spells differently is not applied and is listed under report.refused_detail.awaiting_review_name_not_equal with its confidence.

dictionary.line:
A: GrossOutlayAmountByTAS_CPE | B: The definition for this element appears in Section 20 of OMB Circular A-11 issued June 2015; a brief summary from A-11 appears below.

Payments made to liquidate an obligation (other than the repayment of debt principal or other disbursements that are “means of financing” transactions). Outlays generally are equal to cash disbursements but also are recorded for cash-equivalent transactions, such as the issuance of debentures to pay insurance claims, and in a few cases are recorded on an accrual basis such as interest on public issues of the public debt. Outlays are the measure of Government spending. | C: N/A | D: Account Status | E: N/A | F: N/A | G: N/A | H: N/A | I: N/A | J: N/A | K: FA_AccountBalances.csv,
TAS_AccountBalances.csv | L: gross_outlay_amount | M: appropriation_account_balances | N: gross_outlay_amount_by_tas_cpe | O: N/A | P: N/A | Q: N/A

awaiting_review_api_entity_is_broader.detail: USAspending's bureau is 'Benefits Programs', Treasury's grouping of the compensation, pension, readjustment and insurance accounts the Veterans Benefits Administration administers, at $233bn. That grouping is not the administration, and nothing here establishes that its accounts are exactly this node's.

USAspending's bureau is 'National Security Council and Homeland Security Council', which covers two bodies. The graph carries no Homeland Security Council node, so the key is broader than this node by whatever share of it that council is.
